fact: The ATU secretary general addressed the 11th Africa Spectrum Management Conference in Tunis, attended by the director general of Tunisia's Agence Nationale des Fréquences, whose discussions feed the ATU's Third African Preparatory Meeting for WRC-27 (the report is dated 2026-09-10 and gives no other date).
Tunisia's National Frequency Agency hosted in Tunis the ATU-coordinated Third African Preparatory Meeting for WRC-27, which opened on 2026-09-08 and ran to 11 September, according to the ATU.

Tunisia was elected on 24 July 2026 at the ATU's seventh Conference of Plenipotentiaries in Abuja to the ATU administrative council for 2027-2030, as reported by Assabah News citing the Tunisian foreign ministry.

In a circular dated 2026-07-07 to its member states, the ATU announced that it would hold the 3rd African Preparatory Meeting for WRC-27 in Tunis on 7-11 September 2026 in collaboration with Tunisia's National Frequency Agency; this is an announcement before the meeting took place.

The fourth session of the Algerian-Tunisian Joint Technical Commission on communications and ICT cooperation, held in Tunisia, concluded with agreement on joint projects on connectivity, postal and telecom modernisation and innovation; the report gives no meeting date, so its publication date of 2026-06-09 is used.

Tunisia's National Frequency Agency hosted the Third African Preparatory Meeting for WRC-27 (APM27-3) in Tunis, coordinated by the African Telecommunications Union, with African governments and regulators attending; the document is dated 2026-09-17 and says the four-day meeting began that September.

The Algerian-Tunisian Joint Technical Commission on communications and ICT cooperation held its fourth session in Tunisia on 9 June 2026: a joint body set up under the two governments' cooperation and meeting.
Smart Africa names Tunisia among the 19 signatories of the SATA Declaration on digital trust and cross-border interoperability.
